description: Curated reading lists by named scholars and practitioners. Each entry is a themed annotated bibliography with a clear editorial point of view.

deep_dives.title: Farm Animal Welfare in India
deep_dives.tagline: India has 851 million farmed birds, a Supreme Court judgment that read animal dignity into Article 21, and a cruelty statute whose first-offence fine is still fifty rupees. A reading list on the distance between them.
sections: The Distance Between the Law and the Shed
Does the Welfare Curve Fit India?

deep_dives.title: Water, Sanitation, and the Behaviour Gap
deep_dives.tagline: Why toilets get built and not used, why open defecation persists where people can afford not to, and what actually changes behaviour — a reading list on WASH in South Asia.
sections: Measuring It, and Why It Matters
The India Puzzle: Toilets Without Use
Closing the Gap: Demand, Norms & Behaviour

deep_dives.title: Reading Indian Political Economy
deep_dives.tagline: From colonial legacies to coalition capitalism — a syllabus for understanding how power, markets, and the state co-evolve in India.

deep_dives.title: Impact Measurement: Foundations and Frontiers
deep_dives.tagline: What we measure, why it matters, and where the field is heading — a working syllabus for evaluators.

deep_dives.title: Climate and Just Transitions in South Asia
deep_dives.tagline: Reading climate change as a development question — equity, energy, and the politics of transition.

deep_dives.title: Caste, Identity, and Development
deep_dives.tagline: Why development outcomes track social hierarchy — and what it would take to design programs that don't.

deep_dives.title: Data, Power, and the Global South
deep_dives.tagline: Who counts, who is counted, and who decides — a critical syllabus on data politics in the developing world.

deep_dives.title: SEL Evaluation in India: What Works, What Doesn't, and How
deep_dives.tagline: A working syllabus on Social-Emotional Learning evaluation in Indian school contexts — methods, measures, and the critical scholarship on both.
deep_dives.curator_role: Curated with input from SEL practitioners

deep_dives.title: Cash Transfers and the Evidence
deep_dives.tagline: Conditional or unconditional, cash or kind, delivered how — what two decades of trials actually taught us about giving money to the poor.
sections: The Experimental Core: Just Give Money

deep_dives.title: Climate Adaptation Finance and Loss & Damage
deep_dives.tagline: Who pays to adapt, and who pays for the harm already done — a working reading list on the money behind climate justice.

deep_dives.title: Randomista Economics and Its Critics
deep_dives.tagline: The rise of the randomised trial, the 2019 Nobel, and the long argument about what experiments can and cannot tell us about development.

deep_dives.title: India's Female Labour-Force Puzzle
deep_dives.tagline: Why do so few Indian women work for pay — and why did participation fall as the economy boomed? A guided reading list.
sections: Norms, Care, and the Marriage Market

deep_dives.title: The Learning Crisis
deep_dives.tagline: Children are in school as never before — and learning far less than the world assumed. A reading list on the gap between schooling and learning.

deep_dives.title: Measuring Empowerment
deep_dives.tagline: Beyond income: agency, autonomy, and the trouble with proxies — a working reading list for evaluators measuring something that resists measurement.

deep_dives.title: The Politics of Targeting
deep_dives.tagline: Universal or targeted welfare? A reading list on who gets left out, why "programmes for the poor" so often become poor programmes, and how the technology of identification reshapes the politics.
sections: Foundations: The Case For and Against Targeting
Errors, Proxies, and What Targeting Actually Achieves

deep_dives.title: Health Systems and UHC in South Asia
deep_dives.tagline: How a region of nearly two billion people is trying to reach universal health coverage — and why the money, not just the medicine, is the hard part.
sections: What UHC Means, and How We Measure It
The Indian Diagnosis: Equity, Spending, and the Lancet Series
Ayushman Bharat and the Insurance Bet
Provision, Quality, and the Road Ahead

deep_dives.title: Decolonising Development Knowledge
deep_dives.tagline: Whose evidence counts, who gets to theorise, and what localisation actually demands — a reading list on epistemic justice in development.

deep_dives.title: Informality and Social Protection
deep_dives.tagline: Gig work, the "missing middle", and portable benefits — how informal economies are measured, and how protection can reach the workers who hold them up.
sections: India's Informal Economy & the Missing Middle

deep_dives.title: The Stunting Puzzle
deep_dives.tagline: South Asia's children are among the most stunted in the world, and richer than many who are taller — a reading list on why, and on what actually brings stunting down.

deep_dives.title: The Care Economy
deep_dives.tagline: The unpaid work that holds every economy up — mostly women's, mostly uncounted. A reading list on recognising, reducing, and redistributing care.
sections: Why Care Counts — and Why It Wasn't Counted
Crisis, Pandemic, and the Road Ahead

deep_dives.title: Climate Migration in South Asia
deep_dives.tagline: Floods, salt, heat, and the people who move — and the people who can't. A reading list on climate, displacement, and adaptation across the region most exposed to both.
sections: The Big Picture and the Numbers

deep_dives.title: AI and Development
deep_dives.tagline: The most over-hyped and under-examined tool in the development toolkit. A reading list on what AI can genuinely do for the poor — and what it does to them.
sections: The Promise: AI as a Development Tool
The Peril: Bias, Power, and Extraction
Data Colonialism and the Politics of Data
Infrastructure, Language, and the Road Ahead

deep_dives.title: Platform & Gig Work in India
deep_dives.tagline: Is platform work an escape from informality, or informality with an app? A guided reading list on India's gig economy — the numbers, the worker's day, the law, and the organising.

deep_dives.title: Rural Non-Farm Enterprise in India
deep_dives.tagline: India has 43 million rural enterprises and 93% of them employ nobody. A guided reading list on why so few hire, what the evidence says about fixing it, and which constraint is actually binding.
sections: The Anchor, and How the Counting Works
Women's Enterprise, and What the Gap Is Made Of
Credit, and the Asymmetry in How Failure Is Treated
Markets, Collectives and the Platform Promise
